name: Teaching Dimension / Densest Subgraph (twice)
details: For every finite binary class, teaching dimension dominates twice the density of its densest induced subgraph.
proof: For every nonempty subfamily $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H$, teaching dimension is subfamily-monotonic and at least average teaching dimension. Averaging the pointwise teaching-set/degree lower bound gives $\mathrm{TD}(\mathcal H)\ge\mathrm{TS}_{\mathrm{avg}}(\mathcal G)\ge\mathrm{dens}(\mathcal G)$. Maximizing the final term over subfamilies gives the densest-subgraph parameter.
proof_source: Corollary \ref{cor:teaching-densest-subgraph} in the survey, using Corollary \ref{cor:average-teaching-density}.
witness_verification: For Warmuth's $C_5$ class, the established teaching dimension is $3$ and the densest-subgraph value is $1$.
